glossary.Cartilage: Smooth, rubbery tissue covering the ends of bones in a joint so they glide freely.
glossary.Degeneration: Gradual breakdown and loss of function of a tissue.
glossary.Bilaterally: On both sides of the body.
glossary.Joint insult: Any earlier damage to a joint, such as a fracture or ligament tear.
glossary.Ligament: A tough band joining bone to bone that stabilises a joint.
glossary.Weight-bearing joints: Joints that carry body weight, such as hips, knees and spine.
glossary.Morning stiffness: Joint stiffness on waking; short in OA, over 30 minutes in inflammatory arthritis.
glossary.Palpation: Examining by feeling with the hands.
glossary.Erythema: Redness of the skin from increased blood flow.
glossary.Inflammatory markers: Blood tests such as CRP and ESR that rise with inflammation.
glossary.Nodes: Small, hard bony swellings at the finger joints in OA.
glossary.Rheumatoid arthritis: An autoimmune inflammatory arthritis of small hand and foot joints that spares the DIPs.
glossary.Calf: The back of the lower leg.
glossary.Gold standard: The best available test or treatment against which others are judged.
glossary.Clinical diagnosis: A diagnosis made from history and examination without needing a test.
glossary.Subchondral: The layer of bone just beneath the joint cartilage.
glossary.Ibuprofen: A common NSAID painkiller and anti-inflammatory.
glossary.Diclofenac: An NSAID used as a gel on the skin or as tablets.
glossary.Paracetamol: A simple painkiller; NICE says do not offer it routinely in OA.
glossary.Physiotherapy: Exercise-based treatment to strengthen muscles and keep joints moving.
glossary.Vascular risk factors: Things that raise heart attack and stroke risk, such as smoking, diabetes and hypertension.
glossary.Co-prescribe: Prescribe one drug alongside another, often to protect against side effects.
glossary.Hip replacement: Surgery replacing the femoral head and socket with an artificial joint.
glossary.Posterior dislocation: The ball of the hip slipping out backwards; the leg looks short and turned in.
glossary.Internal rotation: The limb turned inwards towards the midline.
glossary.Foot drop: Inability to lift the front of the foot, from common peroneal nerve damage.
glossary.End-stage disease: The final, most severe stage of a disease, here kidney failure.
glossary.Multidisciplinary: Care shared between several professions, such as doctors, physios and occupational therapists.
glossary.Matrix: The material between cells, in cartilage made of collagen and proteoglycans.
glossary.Remodels: Bone is broken down and rebuilt in a new shape in response to load.
glossary.Sclerosis: Hardening and thickening of bone, seen as whiter areas on X-ray.
glossary.Inflammatory arthritides: Arthritis driven by the immune system, such as rheumatoid or psoriatic arthritis.
glossary.Systemic: Affecting the whole body, such as fever and raised CRP.
glossary.Mechanical loading: The force placed through a joint by weight and movement.
glossary.Herniation: Tissue or fluid bulging out through a weak point.
glossary.Z-thumb: A thumb bent at the MCP and over-extended at the IP joint, typical of RA.
glossary.Rheumatoid nodules: Firm lumps under the skin over pressure points in rheumatoid arthritis.
